title: POC scoping - Private networking & data residency - Verdant Health
summary: Initial POC scoping focused on private connectivity options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), EU data residency, egress constraints and benchmark plan. Customer requires proof-of-concept showing latency and throughput for a chat workload under private networking with SOC2-compliant KMS, plus clear timeline for a 2-week benchmark window.
topics: VPC peering vs AWS PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway
benchmark plan: tokens/sec, p95 latency targets, model variants
security controls: KMS, audit logs, SSO, SOC2
next_steps: Marco to send benchmark config + test scripts (via shared repo) by 2027-03-23
Sophie to share Redwood private networking one-pager and security pack (SOC2, KMS, audit logs) by 2027-03-22
Customer to confirm EU region(s) and provide network contact for VPC peering by 2027-03-24
Set up initial pilot VPC peering/PrivateLink connection and schedule 2-week benchmark starting 2027-03-29
action_items: Marco - provide sample benchmark config, load profile and scripts (due 2027-03-23)
Sophie - share security docs & price estimate for dedicated pilot (due 2027-03-22)
Ravi - confirm which EU region(s) can be used and send network peering contact (due 2027-03-24)
Emily - list compliance constraints (data residency, retention) and firewall rules needed (due 2027-03-24)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-03-21 16:00 PT
Duration: 46m
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lena Brooks (Redwood Solutions), Dana Price (Verdant CTO), Ravi Patel (Verdant Cloud), Emily Lawson (Verdant Security), Tom Nguyen (Verdant PM)

Auto-summary: quick round on goals - private networking and EU data residency, want concrete benchmark and security pack, agree next steps.

[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Sophie with Redwood, i'll kick off - quick roll call, looks like we have the Verdant folks on, do you want to intro quickly Dana?
[00:15] Dana: yeah hi, Dana price here, CTO at Verdant, we're evaluating inference platforms for our patient-facing chat and notes summarization, primary blockers are residency in EU and no public egress of PHI, so private connectivity is key.
[00:34] Ravi: hey all, i'm ravi, cloud eng, i'll own peering and network work, short on time but want to get details on routing and egress.
[00:44] Emily: emily, security lead - SOC2 in place, need to validate KMS integration and audit logs, want to see how token retention/retention policies are handled.
[00:59] Sophie: great, thanks. Marco and i will walk through options and propose a benchmark. Marco over to you for the technical side.
[01:12] Marco: cool thanks, so at a high level we typically support three private connectivity patterns for POCs: cross-account VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) and if needed a transit gateway pattern for larger networks. for EU-only residency we can pin the control plane and serving in eu-west-1 or eu-central-1 depending on your preference.
[01:40] Tom: quick q - what's the difference operationally between peering and PrivateLink for us?
[01:46] Marco: peering is L3 routed between VPCs, simpler, but requires CIDR management and routes in both accounts; PrivateLink uses interface ENIs in your VPC and keeps traffic on AWS backbone and is cross-account without opening routing tables, so often preferred for stricter egress control. there's tradeoffs around ephemeral IPs and scaling.
[02:10] Ravi: will PrivateLink require us to open inbound rules for those ENIs or is it outbound only?
[02:16] Marco: it's basically your VPC creating an interface endpoint and we provision the service side - you control SGs on the ENI, so you can restrict to specific subnets and ports. it avoids peering CIDR collisions.
[02:32] Emily: regarding egress, we cannot allow any traffic leaving EU to internet, even for model updates, is that supported?
[02:39] Marco: yes we can lock the deployment to EU regions; for model uploads and library updates we can pull from mirrors in region or provide an offline image for on-prem style if needed. also we support customer-hosted KMS via x.509 and HSM integration for keys so key material stays under your control.
[03:00] Dana: latency targets - for chat we want p95 < 300ms ideally when in eu region, throughput about 20 concurrent users per instance, and cost targets matter but first we want to prove feasibility.
[03:18] Marco: noted. for benchmarking we'll propose a steady-state scenario and a burst profile; rough numbers - on a single A100-style GPU we typically see X tokens/sec depending on model - (note: transcription: 'X' placeholder, we'll send exact numbers in benchmark doc).
[03:36] Sophie: also note we have dedicated options if you want reserved capacity which helps with predictable throughput and private networking.
[03:45] Ravi: what about NAT and egress charges? if traffic stays inside AWS region but across accounts, any egress cost?
[03:52] Marco: cross-AZ or cross-account within same region is typically free or low cost on AWS; traffic to the internet will incur egress. PrivateLink keeps things regional and on the AWS backbone so minimal egress to internet. we'll include a cost estimate for data transfer in the POC doc.
[04:10] Emily: audit logs - can we ship full request/response logs to our SIEM over a private link? we cannot have logs transiting public internet.
[04:20] Marco: yes you can push logs to your CloudWatch or a customer-managed S3 in the same region over the private connection; we can support cross-account roles and S3 bucket policies. we also provide structured telemetry in the console.
[04:36] Tom: success criteria - what should we measure?
[04:40] Sophie: we'll propose success criteria: 1) connectivity established via PrivateLink or peering; 2) p95 latency under target for chat workload (we'll baseline model variants); 3) tokens/sec throughput sustained for X users; 4) security checklist verified (KMS, audit logs, SOC2 materials); 5) runbook for scaling.
[05:05] Dana: timeline? we'd like to start bench by end of month, two week run.
[05:10] Sophie: target start 2027-03-29 for the 2-week benchmark. Marco will share configs by 3/23 so you can prep network.
[05:20] Marco: on benchmarks - i'll include exact model variants (redwood-rl1, open-quant-2) and suggested sequence lengths; default chat seq 256, we can test up to 2k to see degradation. also will include KV cache warmup procedures.
[05:38] Ravi: do you need any changes to our NAT or firewall? we usually block outbound except certain whitelisted endpoints.
[05:44] Marco: for PrivateLink you'll need to allow ENI communications and the service endpoints; we'll provide the IP ranges and ports. if you go peering we'll need route updates.
[05:55] Emily: data retention - can we configure no-text retention for PHI and only store telemetry?
[06:01] Marco: yes retention is configurable per-tenant; we can set zero retention of full transcripts and only store metrics, and any slow logs can be forwarded to your bucket encrypted with your KMS.
[06:15] Dana: curious about fallback - if dedicated nodes are saturated do you offer a fallback to hosted to keep availability?
[06:23] Sophie: yes we have routing policies that can failover to another variant or lower-cost hosted model but that may cross boundaries - for your case we can keep failover within EU and within private connectivity options to meet residency. we'll document failover policy in the POC runbook.
[06:40] Tom: any regulatory issues with PrivateLink in EU?
[06:44] Marco: as long as the service and storage are provisioned in EU regions and keys are customer-managed, we align with common residency controls; we'll include our compliance pack.
[06:55] Sophie: let's talk about benchmarks numbers quickly - Marco, can you call out the target p95 for a mid-sized model?
[07:02] Marco: rough expected p95 for a 7B-class model in eu-west-1 under private link and single GPU - ballpark 120-250ms depending on prompt length; larger models will be higher. again exact values in the doc.
[07:20] Emily: we also need proof that logs and any model telemetry do not leave eu-west-1.
[07:25] Marco: we'll ensure S3 buckets, CloudWatch and telemetry endpoints are regional; we can also restrict egress to those endpoints.
[07:36] Ravi: network test plan? do you provide an agent to run throughput tests from our VPC?
[07:40] Marco: yes we'll supply a simple tester and a k6-type load script that runs from an EC2 in your VPC hitting the private endpoint. it will measure RPS, p95, and token throughput.
[07:52] Dana: how do we validate encryption at rest and in transit?
[07:56] Marco: in transit uses TLS mutual for PrivateLink, and at rest we integrate with your KMS; we can provide attestation and cert chains.
[08:07] Sophie: ok let's map responsibilities - Marco will author bench plan, Sophie will send price and security pack, Verdant will provision network contact and test VPC.
[08:18] Emily: one more ask - can you provide a sample data flow diagram we can include in the change request?
[08:24] Marco: yes i'll include an architecture diagram for PrivateLink and peering options.
[08:30] Tom: any blockers on our side? we need to confirm budget but will treat this as a pilot.
[08:36] Sophie: understood. we'll keep the pilot scoped so cost is predictable.
[08:42] Dana: ok thanks, that covers it, schedule follow-up next week after you send docs.
[08:48] Sophie: thanks everyone, we'll email the artifacts and confirm the 3/29 start if all good.
[08:54] (call wraps, some crosstalk)

Notes about transcription quality: a few model names were garbled during the call (we referenced placeholders 'X' and some model names were off), proper names will be clarified in follow-up doc.

References shared: "Redwood private networking one-pager" (link: https://redwood.example/links/p1), "POC benchmark config (placeholder)" (will be shared repo link), security pack (link coming).

End of transcript.
